4.0.0.en: 1 But in the last days it shall come to pass, that the mountain of the house of the LORD shall be established in the top of the mountains, and it shall be exalted above the hills; and people shall flow unto it.

4.0.1.en: The prophet Micah looks toward the fullness of time, when God the Word becomes incarnate to raise up from humanity not a lofty mountain like Mount Horeb, where the prophet Moses received the Law, but the mountain of mountains, whose summit reaches heaven itself. For the Heavenly One came to raise up from the fallen a glorious Church of towering height, bearing the citizenship of her heavenly Bridegroom.

4.0.2.en: An American child, proud of his nationality, wrote a letter addressed to God, in which he said: "I am an American, and what about You?" He is the Heavenly One who calls every believer to be united with Him and to bear His citizenship, so that all sing with the Apostle Paul: "[He] hath made us sit together in heavenly places."

4.0.3.en: But in the last days it shall come to pass, that the mountain of the house of the LORD shall be established in the top of the mountains, and it shall be exalted above the hills; and people shall flow unto it. [1]

4.0.4.en: What is stated in verses [1-3] is almost identical to what is stated in the Book of Isaiah (Isa 2:2-4). Since the two were contemporaries, though Isaiah was older than Micah, some think that the latter quoted this from the former, while some scholars think that both quoted from a third source, under the guidance of the Holy Spirit of God.

4.0.5.en: The expression "in the last days" is usually used by the prophets to point to the messianic age (Hos 3:5).

4.0.6.en: * (The prophet Isaiah 2:2) He prophesies of a glorious and widespread manifestation of godliness among all who dwell round about: the destruction of the idols, with the house of the Lord enjoying the universal character that befits it. For by the mountains and hills he means not only the removal of the errors that had reigned over everyone, after the appearing of our Savior, when the falsehood of the idols was exposed, but he also announced the beauty of the truth, and thus we see the prophecy being fulfilled. Add to this the saying "in the last days," by which he means "the days that follow the appearing of the Lord."

4.0.7.en: Theodoret, Bishop of Cyrus. Many of the Fathers of the Church see that this glorious mountain refers to the Church of the New Testament, among them St. Cyril the Great, St. John Chrysostom and Eusebius of Caesarea.

4.0.8.en: * Paul said the same thing: "The fullness of the time was come" (Gal 4:4), and in another place: "that in the dispensation of the fulness of times" (Isa 2:2). He points to the Church and the firmness of her teachings like a mountain... What is marvelous about the Church is not that she is victorious, but the manner in which she became so. She is pursued and persecuted, and torn in a thousand ways, and yet not only does she not diminish, but she has become great, and by enduring sufferings she shatters those who try to pour blows upon her. This is the work of the pearl that is struck with iron: it exhausts the strength of those who strike it... So when the prophet depicts her as a mountain, he means by this the strength of the Church, her steadfastness, her loftiness and her endurance...

4.0.9.en: "And all nations shall flow unto it." Notice here how the prophet not only announced the call directed to the Gentiles, but also their eagerness to respond to the call. He did not say "they will be driven," but "they will come."

4.0.10.en: St. John Chrysostom. Is not all humanity, the one flock, God's? Is not God Himself the Lord of all peoples and their Shepherd?

4.0.11.en: Tertullian the scholar. The Church is raised to the top of the mountains, that is, she reaches the heights of heaven, where she bears the heavenly nature by her union with the heavenly Head. And she is exalted above the hills, where she passes over every earthly standard and human thought, rising above all human philosophies, cultures and arts, for she is not the making of men, but the work of the hands of the Almighty Himself.

4.0.12.en: "People shall flow unto it": this does not apply to the Jewish temple, which was closed to the Gentiles; but the Church, from the very beginning of her going forth, the Lord called His disciples to go and teach the nations (Mt 28:19).

4.0.13.en: Some of the Fathers see that the mountain of the house of the Lord is the Lord Christ, who is established in the top of the mountains, that is, above all the prophets. This mountain is the rock on which the Church of the New Testament is founded.

4.0.14.en: * The prophet Micah presented Christ under the symbol of a great mountain, speaking thus: "But in the last days the mountain of the house of the LORD..." (Mic 4:2-3).

4.1.s.en: 2. A people of peoples and a divine school:

4.1.0.en: 2 And many nations shall come, and say, Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, and to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for the law shall go forth of Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.

4.1.1.en: The Jews considered that there was no salvation for anyone unless he became a Jew, and that all the other peoples had no relationship with God, since they alone were the chosen people of God. They did not realize that God, who chose them to be a holy leaven, chose all the nations to ascend, with Christ who ascended into the heavens, to the mountain of the Lord, to heaven itself.

4.1.2.en: If God raises up from every believing heart a holy temple for Himself, it is only so that the Law of the New Testament may go forth from Jerusalem, the word of the Lord that attracts every tongue and nation, so that all may enjoy the Word, the Giver of life and resurrection. The Church has become the people of peoples, gathering from all the nations a holy, heavenly people.

4.1.3.en: She is a divine school whose head is the unique divine Teacher; He carries His disciples in Himself and dwells in their depths, so that they receive fellowship in the divine nature.

4.1.4.en: And many nations shall come, and say,

4.1.5.en: Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, and to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths:

4.1.6.en: for the law shall go forth of Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem. [2]

4.1.7.en: The nations will come to the Church of the New Testament, the mountain of the Lord and the house of the God of Jacob, so that all may enjoy the prophecies and types in the Law concerning the Lord Christ and His work of salvation.

4.1.8.en: In the letter of Pope Athanasius to Epictetus, bishop of Jerusalem, he quotes this passage to speak of the coming of the incarnate Word of the Lord from Jerusalem, explaining that the Word was not changed into flesh and bones and hair and the whole body, nor did He change from His divine nature by His incarnation.

4.1.9.en: * From here (Jerusalem) every place in the world has experienced joy; from here come happiness and delight, from here the sources of sound thought; here Christ was crucified, and from here the Apostles set out... This delight is immortal.

4.1.10.en: St. John Chrysostom. * The prophet Micah used the symbol of the high mountain to speak of the gathering of the nations in Christ [he cites (Mic 4:1-3)]... After that the same prophet told us beforehand even the place where Christ was born (Mic 5:2).

4.1.11.en: St. Augustine. * Micah announced that the new Law would be given in the following way: "The law shall go forth of Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem. And he shall judge among many people, and shall conquer nations and rebuke them." For the first Law, which was given through Moses, was not given on Mount Zion but on Mount Horeb. And the Sibyl showed that this would come to an end through the Son of God. "But when all these things are fulfilled of which he spoke at that time, the whole Law (in its letter) will be abolished."

4.1.12.en: Lactantius. * When the prophetic Spirit spoke, prophesying of the things to come, he said: "The law shall go forth of Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem, and he shall judge among the nations, and many people shall be rebuked. And they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks, nation shall not lift up a sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more." We can show you that this has indeed truly happened. For a company of twelve men went out from Jerusalem, who were common and untrained in speech. But by the power of God they bore witness to Christ in order to teach all the word of God. And now we who used to kill one another not only do not make war against one another, but, so as not to lie and not to deceive our judges, we gladly die for the confession of Christ; for it has become possible for us to follow the saying: "The tongue swears while the mind remains unsworn." But it is folly for the soldiers who were enlisted by you and whose names were registered to remain in loyalty to you instead of loyalty to their lives and their parents and their country and all their families. For you have nothing incorruptible to offer to those who desire incorruption. Rather we bear all things in order to receive what we desire from the One who is able to grant it.

4.1.13.en: St. Justin. * Behold, you see that they will be choirs and keep festivals, each encouraging the other, and all became teachers, not one nation nor two nor three nations... but all gather together. He says: many peoples came from different lands. This never happened at all with the Jews; if a few came, they were a few proselytes who came with great difficulty, and they never took the name of the nations, but came as proselytes.

4.1.14.en: St. John Chrysostom. * The great David says to you: "O come, let us rejoice in the Lord" (Ps 95:1), or another prophet says: "Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD" (Mic 4:2), or the Savior Himself says: "Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest" (Mt 11:28), or: Arise for plunder, shining with splendor, gleaming more than snow, whiter than milk (see Lam 4:7), shining more than sapphire; let us not resist nor delay!

4.1.15.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus. * After the experience of the troubles in which they will find themselves, when first the Assyrians and later the Babylonians take them captive, a great change will take place with regard to this place, the mountain that is thought to be where God dwells, as it becomes famous and is shown to surpass all mountains, to rise above all the mountains and hills because of the glory that covers it through divine compassion. Great numbers from all places, even from foreign peoples, will hasten to gather and reach the mountain of God, where God is thought to dwell, and they will learn how they ought to order their lives as is fitting.

4.1.16.en: Theodore of Mopsuestia. * The divine Gospel preaching reaches to the ends of the earth, according to the prophecy of the Lord recorded in the holy Gospels: "[This gospel of the kingdom] shall be preached ... for a witness unto all nations" [see Mt 24:14]. And He urged the holy Apostles with the words: "Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you" (Mt 28:19-20). This Gospel Law and Apostolic preaching began at Jerusalem as from a spring and reached the whole world, providing irrigation for those who draw near to the faith.

4.1.17.en: * "For the law shall go forth of Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem." The prophet speaks here of a new Law and a new word, because the old Law was given at Sinai, but the Law of the New Testament was delivered at Zion. The first was delivered to the Jews alone, but the new was delivered to all peoples and nations, to the whole human race. God gave the old Law not at Zion, but on Mount Sinai. It is very clear that he is pointing to the New Testament. There it was given first to the Apostles, and thanks to them, as they carried it to all the nations.

4.2.0.en: 3 And he shall judge among many people, and rebuke strong nations afar off; and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up a sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.

4.2.1.en: After speaking of the Church as the firm mountain of mountains, and as a unique school under the leadership of the divine Teacher, the Lord of glory Jesus, he tells us of her as a marvelous and unique court in which the Judge, the Savior of the world, is enthroned, not to destroy and take vengeance, but to renew human nature by His Holy Spirit, and so grant heavenly peace and surpassing harmony. Instead of the battle between soul and body, and between mind and human passions, His surpassing peace reigns over the whole being of man, so that he becomes a harp of the Spirit that sends forth a song of heavenly love, proclaiming the accomplishment of reconciliation with God, as with men and with the heavenly beings.

4.2.2.en: And he shall judge among many people,

4.2.3.en: and rebuke strong nations afar off; and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks:

4.2.4.en: nation shall not lift up a sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more. [3]

4.2.5.en: * Since the coming of the Lord, the New Testament has restored peace, and the Law that gives life has gone forth to all the earth, as the prophets said.

4.2.6.en: St. Irenaeus. * Who is this that does so, or who is it that unites men in peace, who hated one another, except the beloved Son of the Father, the common Savior of all, Jesus Christ, who by His love undertook all things for our salvation? For from of old the peace that He brings in was foretold, as the Scripture says: "They shall beat their swords into plowshares."

4.2.7.en: Pope Athanasius the Apostolic. What are these swords but the passions, feelings and energies which we used to use to kill our souls and the souls of those attached to us? For through the spiritual peace that the Savior grants us, all these energies are turned into plowshares for our souls, which till our hearts, removing the stones and thorns and turning our inner wilderness into a spiritual garden full of the fruit of the Spirit.

4.2.8.en: Man no longer learns war against his brother, but enjoys peace without fear (Zech 3:10).

4.3.0.en: 4 But they shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree; and none shall make them afraid: for the mouth of the LORD of hosts hath spoken it. 5 For all people will walk every one in the name of his god, and we will walk in the name of the LORD our God for ever and ever.

4.3.1.en: The Lord planted the garden of Eden so that Adam and his sons might live under the tree of life, to eat and be satisfied, and to sit and rest in the Lord. But man soon drove himself out of the garden to live in the valley of tears, groaning under the weight of the sin he chose with his full free will, and he became its abject slave. Now that our Christ has come, He has established His Church as a joyful divine garden, in which His sons (the sons of the second Adam) may live. The believer sits under the vine and rests under the fig tree. What is the vine but the Lord Christ, crucified and risen from the dead, the source of true joy, the wine of the New Testament? And what is the fig tree but the Holy Spirit, the Giver of love, who binds believers together like the seeds of the fig, which give a sweet taste and are enclosed in a covering of unity that holds the seeds within?

4.3.2.en: It is a unique garden in which we eat and drink of the Body and Blood of the Lord, and are watered by His Holy Spirit, the living water!

4.3.3.en: But they shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree; and none shall make them afraid: for the mouth of the LORD of hosts hath spoken it. [4]

4.3.4.en: Sitting under the shade is a symbolic expression used to indicate the peace of the nation and local happiness (see 1 Kgs 4:25; Zech 3:10). This was based on the custom that prevailed, that a person would seek a pleasant shade under fig trees and vines. In the East the vine is used more for ornament and for shade than ivy in the West. The branches are trained to make a trellis in the courtyard of the house. Fig trees, with their massive branches and broad leaves, provide a natural shade that delights the soul.

4.3.5.en: * The Song of Songs alludes to (the vine and the fig tree of the field) in this way: "I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and virtues of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please" (Song 2:7) LXX.

4.3.6.en: This is the field (of righteousness) full of peace itself, of which the Lord also speaks in the Psalm: "Whatsoever moves in the field is mine" (Ps 50:11) LXX. In this field is the vine that is pressed and gives forth blood, and washes and purifies the world. And in this field is the tree under which the saints sit to rest, and are renewed by good spiritual grace. In this field the fruitful olive tree is crushed, and gives the oil of the Lord's peace. In this field the pomegranate trees (Song 8:2) flourish, shading much fruit in the bosom of the one faith and sending into it the warmth of love.

4.3.7.en: St. Ambrose. * The vine in not a few places refers to the Lord Himself (Jn 15:1), and the fig tree to the Holy Spirit, since the Lord "makes glad the heart of man" (Ps 104:5), and the Holy Spirit heals it. Hezekiah was commanded to make a plaster of a lump of figs, that is, of the fruit of the Spirit, so that he might be healed. And as the Apostle says of this healing, it begins with love: "But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance" (Gal 5:22-23). Because of the greatness of their delight, the prophet calls these spiritual fruits figs. Micah also says of them: "They shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree; and none shall make them afraid" (Mic 4:4). Surely whoever takes refuge in the Spirit and rests under Him, and under the shadow of the Word, is not frightened or terrified by anyone who causes trouble to human hearts.

4.3.8.en: Methodius. * We read in Genesis that God planted a garden eastward, and there He put the man whom He had formed (Gen 2:8). Who has the power to create a paradise but God Almighty, who "spake, and it was done" (Ps 33:9), and who never had need of what He willed to bring into being? He planted this paradise, of which He says that it is His wisdom: "Every plant, which my heavenly Father hath not planted, shall be rooted up" (Mt 15:13). It is a good planting, for it was said of the angels and the saints that they rest under the fig tree and the vine. In this matter there is a symbol of the angels in the time of the peace to come.

4.3.9.en: St. Ambrose. For all people will walk every one in the name of his god, and we will walk in the name of the LORD our God for ever and ever.

4.4.0.en: Those who walk in the name of the Lord will have eternal peace. [5]

4.4.1.en: * Those who are eager to ascend the mountain of the Lord, and desire to learn His ways, promise readiness for obedience, and so receive within them the glories of life in Christ, and pledge with all their strength to be zealous in all holiness. He says: "In every country and city let each one walk in the way he chooses and worship as seems good to him; but our concern is Christ, and we make His law a straight path, in which we walk with Him, not only in this present life or in the past but, what is greater, in what lies beyond it." It is a faithful saying: "Those who suffer with Him will walk with Him forever, and with Him be glorified, and with Him reign" (see 2 Tim 2:11-12; Rom 8:17). But those who prefer nothing to His love make Christ their concern; these cease from the distraction of the vain world and seek rather righteousness and what is pleasing to Him, and to excel in virtue. Such was Paul, when he wrote: "I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me" (Gal 2:19-20). And again: "For I determined not to know any thing among you, save Jesus Christ, and him crucified" (1 Cor 2:2).

4.5.0.en: 6 In that day, saith the LORD, will I assemble her that halteth, and I will gather her that is driven out, and her that I have afflicted;

4.5.1.en: The wisdom of God incarnate was accused of being out of His mind, and was driven out of the camp to be crucified outside Jerusalem. There He stretched out His hands to embrace everyone who is broken, wounded, crushed and outcast! He is the Lord of the rejected. His own did not receive Him, that He might receive within Himself those who have nowhere to lay their heads. He is the Father of the fatherless, the Judge of the widows, the support of the persecuted, and the refuge of those who have no one to ask after them.

4.5.2.en: In that day, saith the LORD, will I assemble her that halteth, and I will gather her that is driven out, and her that I have afflicted; [6]

4.5.3.en: Here he prophesies of the return from captivity, when the nation had become outcast. After the chastening the Lord brings back the outcasts and binds up their wounds.

4.5.4.en: The outcasts become a chosen remnant, the strong people of God (Isa 37:32; 46:3; Jer 23:3; Amos 5:15).

4.6.0.en: 7 And I will make her that halted a remnant, and her that was cast far off a strong nation: and the LORD shall reign over them in mount Zion from henceforth, even for ever. 8 And thou, O tower of the flock, the strong hold of the daughter of Zion, unto thee shall it come, even the first dominion; the kingdom shall come to the daughter of Jerusalem.

4.6.1.en: The prophet Ezekiel marveled when he saw the dry bones become an exceeding great army (Ezek 37:10). It is a vision of every day, in which the Lord Christ raises up from the weak, the ignorant and the despised a great tower that shelters the flock and protects it from the ravening wolves, and a great hill on which the serpent cannot crawl to strike its fangs into the heel of the children of God, and a royal throne on which the King of kings is enthroned to reign over the daughter of the heavenly Jerusalem, His holy Church.

4.6.2.en: * Now it is clear that no one in the whole world can frighten us or subdue us who believe in Jesus. Even though our heads are cut off and we are crucified and thrown to wild beasts and bound and burned, and endure every other kind of torture, it is evident that we do not deny the confession of our faith.

4.6.3.en: The more we are persecuted, the more the number of those who receive the faith increases and become worshippers of God in the name of Jesus. Just as one cuts off the branches of a fruitful vine and it grows again and puts forth other fruitful shoots, so it happens with the Christians, for the vine is planted by God and Christ is the Savior of His people. But the rest of the prophecy will be fulfilled at the Second Coming. The prophet Micah says: "In that day, saith the LORD, will I assemble her that halteth (the bruised), and I will gather her that is driven out, and her that I have rejected." This indicates that you do not have the last word, when you and all the other people who have authority wished to drive every Christian out not only from his possessions but even from the whole world, since you do not allow a Christian man to live.

4.6.4.en: St. Justin the Martyr. And I will make her that halted a remnant, and her that was cast far off a strong nation: and the LORD shall reign over them in mount Zion from henceforth, even for ever. [7]

4.7.0.en: And thou, O tower of the flock, the strong hold of the daughter of Zion, unto thee shall it come, even the first dominion; the kingdom shall come to the daughter of Jerusalem. [8]

4.7.1.en: When Jerusalem returns to greater splendor and strength, she becomes like a high tower from which the Good Shepherd tends His flock.

4.7.2.en: * "And thou, O tower, shepherd of the standing daughter of Zion, thy time shall come." These words refer to Zedekiah, the impious king, whom the prophet calls a tower because the people of Judah settled under his shade, and he calls him a shepherd because of his governance of the kingdom, and he calls him dark because of the error of idolatry to which he clung. Again, in the symbolic meaning of his words, he calls Satan a dark shepherd, for in a symbolic way he was always attacking the daughter of Zion under a dark sky. And when he hunts her he drags her away from the light, for truly he who walks in wickedness hates the light. But in the end the lofty, rightful Prince of the symbolic Jerusalem broke this tyrant by His coming, when He drew the dark shepherd away.

4.8.0.en: 9 Now why dost thou cry out aloud? is there no king in thee? is thy counsellor perished? for pangs have taken thee as a woman in travail. 10 Be in pain, and labour to bring forth, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail: for now shalt thou go forth out of the city, and thou shalt dwell in the field, and thou shalt go even to Babylon; there shalt thou be delivered; there the LORD shall redeem thee from the hand of thine enemies. 11 Now also many nations are gathered against thee, that say, Let her be defiled, and let our eye look upon Zion. 12 But they know not the thoughts of the LORD, neither understand they his counsel: for he shall gather them as the sheaves into the floor.

4.8.1.en: If the Church is exposed to continual persecutions, so that she appears as one taken captive, yet her Bridegroom is the Redeemer, who saves her from her enemy, as He brought the ancient people out of Egypt and freed them from the slavery of Pharaoh. And as He brought His people back from the Babylonian captivity with a strong and wondrous hand!

4.8.2.en: Since the Jews interpreted God's promise to King David that his offspring would reign forever, they thought that Judah would never lack a king from the offspring of David. Therefore the words of the prophet Micah about the Babylonian captivity, a century and a half before it happened, were extremely alarming, especially since the false prophets were proclaiming smooth words, affirming God's protection of the city of Jerusalem and its unique temple and the continuance of the kingdom of David, who was of the tribe of Judah.

4.8.3.en: Now why dost thou cry out aloud?

4.8.4.en: is there no king in thee? is thy counsellor perished? for pangs have taken thee as a woman in travail. [9]

4.8.5.en: Be in pain, and labour to bring forth, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail: for now shalt thou go forth out of the city, and thou shalt dwell in the field, and thou shalt go even to Babylon; there shalt thou be delivered;

4.9.0.en: there the LORD shall redeem thee from the hand of thine enemies. [10]

4.9.1.en: Salvation is accomplished through chastening, as God permits Jerusalem to be without a king, like a woman in labor who suffers to bring forth a new child. It was necessary for Judah to be taken captive to Babylon and then return, to enjoy freedom and the return to the land of promise.

4.9.2.en: * Writhe and groan, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in labor, "for now shalt thou go forth out of the city, and thou shalt dwell in the open country (the wilderness); and thou shalt go even to Babylon; there shalt thou be delivered." The meaning is that you will go into captivity, O (people of) Zion, you will be exiled in Babylon, but after years you will return from there, not with a soldier who hurries you along, but with that Commander who, by His ascent into heaven, leads captivity captive. You will follow Him with the brethren with hands joined, and with the commanders of our army who take captive every mind for the sake of Christ.

4.9.3.en: St. Ephrem the Syrian. Now also many nations are gathered against thee, that say,

4.10.0.en: Let her be defiled, and let our eye look upon Zion. [11]

4.10.1.en: When the pagan nations look at captive Jerusalem under chastening, they mock her and curse her, expecting her complete destruction. But these do not understand God's plan and His ordering. The nations will gather together against God and His people in a decisive battle (Joel 3; Ezek 38-39; Zech 12; Rev 20:8 etc.).

4.10.2.en: * Now many nations are gathered against thee. That is, at the same time a mixture of many different nations attacks you under the leadership of Gog. Again there will be a defiling in Zion, and the eye looks upon it, that is, the holy place of Zion will be defiled and utterly despised by those who do not know that they will be threshed by the vengeance of God's justice like the straw that is gathered on the threshing floor.

4.11.0.en: St. Ephrem the Syrian. But they know not the thoughts of the LORD, neither understand they his counsel: for he shall gather them as the sheaves into the floor. [12]

4.11.1.en: The prophet asks us not to search into future events out of a desire to satisfy our curiosity, but to learn the purposes and plans of the Lord concerning us.

4.12.0.en: 13 Arise and thresh, O daughter of Zion: for I will make thine horn iron, and I will make thy hoofs brass: and thou shalt beat in pieces many people: and I will consecrate their gain unto the LORD, and their substance unto the Lord of the whole earth.

4.12.1.en: The prophet David looked toward the Bridegroom of the Church, fairer than the children of men, and saw Him as a commander bearing His sword upon His thigh, going forth conquering and to conquer. Thus the bride of the Commander has her horn of iron and her hoofs of brass; she crushes the hosts of demons under her feet, and offers many souls to the Lord as true, surpassing riches.

4.12.2.en: Arise and thresh, O daughter of Zion: for I will make thine horn iron, and I will make thy hoofs brass: and thou shalt beat in pieces many people: and I will consecrate their gain unto the LORD, and their substance unto the Lord of the whole earth. [13]

4.12.3.en: Now He gives us final victory, in which she crushes the enemy of good, and all events are turned to the glory of the Lord.

4.12.4.en: * "I will make thy horn, which the Babylonians broke, iron, and thou shalt beat in pieces many people, and thou shalt dedicate their produce to the Lord." This will happen after you possess their land and their wealth, and pay tithes to the Lord for the whole earth. As I said, God showed a sign of such great prosperity for the Jews who returned from the captivity. He has kept this very thing for the Church.

4.13.s.en: You have made Your people a wonder!

4.13.0.en: * Who is like You, O God, who forgive sins and give the Kingdom?

4.13.1.en: You have made of Your Church a wonder!

4.13.2.en: And You have shown Your power in me, as a member of Your unique Church!

4.13.3.en: * You have made of me, the weak and crushed, a lofty mountain, whose head is in heaven!

4.13.4.en: You have counted me Your fat mountain, the delight of the heavenly ones!

4.13.5.en: You are King of kings and Lord of lords; You have counted me the mountain of mountains, exceedingly high!

4.13.6.en: You have counted me a member of Your holy Church!

4.13.7.en: * You have made her a unique school with a heavenly Teacher.

4.13.8.en: She gathers disciples from every nation and people and tongue.

4.13.9.en: I have become a member in her, learning from You the language of heaven!

4.13.10.en: I speak the language of heavenly love by my fellowship with You, O Love. My soul praises You, for no fears come upon me.

4.13.11.en: In Your Church, the icon of heaven, I do not suffer from any inability in relationships.

4.13.12.en: For all learn in the language of love.

4.13.13.en: And none suffers from ignorance of the language or inability to speak.

4.13.14.en: You are wonderful, O heavenly Teacher!

4.13.15.en: You have made me beautiful in You, and I carry You within me.

4.13.16.en: You are in my heart as in my mouth; I speak of You continually!

4.13.17.en: * I no longer long for the garden of Eden like my father Adam.

4.13.18.en: For You have established for me a divine garden.

4.13.19.en: I pick the grapes of joy from You, O divine Vine!

4.13.20.en: I pick sweet, satisfying figs from Your Holy Spirit!

4.13.21.en: You have turned my depths into Your garden.

4.13.22.en: I see You with Your Father and Your Holy Spirit, the secret of my joy!

4.13.23.en: * I do not groan at the injustice that prevails in the world!

4.13.24.en: I see You driven out of the camp, and I find glory in being driven out with You, to bear Your cross!

4.13.25.en: You stretch out Your hands on the cross, and so embrace those who have no place in the hearts of others; You draw the poor, You who became poor to enrich us by Your poverty.

4.13.26.en: You draw the suffering, You who were crucified to give the sufferings of love a surpassing sweetness!

4.13.27.en: You embrace the lost, You who became the way that carries us to the divine bosom!

4.13.28.en: You receive the rejected to grant them fellowship in the heavenly glories!

4.13.29.en: * How often my soul has loathed my body because of its lusts!

4.13.30.en: How often my depths have groaned because of my trivial thoughts!

4.13.31.en: How often my heart has cried out because of my unruly passions!

4.13.32.en: Glory to You, O Sanctifier of my whole being!

4.13.33.en: You took a body that I might take pride in Your sanctification of my body!

4.13.34.en: You have given me Your Holy Spirit to govern my thoughts.

4.13.35.en: You have sanctified my passions and consecrated them as a throne for Your love!

4.13.36.en: You have established Your heavenly Kingdom in my depths!

4.13.37.en: You have turned my heart into Your radiant throne!

4.13.38.en: * Why art thou cast down, O my soul, within me? Hope in the Lord, the Redeemer!

4.13.39.en: Pharaoh has no authority to humble me, nor has Babylon the power to shut the doors of captivity upon me!

4.13.40.en: My Redeemer is the liberator of my soul, the Giver of victory to my depths!

4.13.41.en: * Behold, I see Satan fallen from heaven like lightning!

4.13.42.en: He has no place in me, for the Redeemer has made me a heaven!

4.13.43.en: I do not occupy my mind with you; you have no place except under my feet!

4.13.44.en: My Savior has given me authority over you, O weak one!

4.13.45.en: * My soul will lament no more, for my heavenly Bridegroom has made me a glorious Church!

4.13.46.en: He has made me, the dry bones, an exceeding great army!

4.13.47.en: In my Savior I have become Jerusalem, the army with banners!

4.13.48.en: Glory to You, O Bridegroom of the Church, her Savior and her Commander!
